claim: There are thousands of Mendelian diseases with more being discovered weekly.
source: There are thousands of Mendelian diseases with more being discovered weekly and the majority have no approved treatments.
evidence: This is a general statement about the state of Mendelian diseases, drawing from established scientific knowledge about rare genetic diseases.

claim: The majority of Mendelian diseases have no approved treatments.
source: There are thousands of Mendelian diseases with more being discovered weekly and the majority have no approved treatments.
evidence: This statement is supported by citation in the introduction section.

claim: High-throughput imaging and quantitative phenotyping can be conducted systematically on a panel of C. elegans disease model strains.
source: Here, we show that high-throughput imaging and quantitative phenotyping can be conducted systematically on a panel of C. elegans disease model strains.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: 25 worm models of human Mendelian diseases were created using CRISPR genome-editing.
source: We used CRISPR genome-editing to create 25 worm models of human Mendelian diseases and phenotyped them using a single standardised assay.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and supported by the methods and results sections.

claim: All but two strains were significantly different from wild-type controls in at least one feature.
source: All but two strains were significantly different from wild-type controls in at least one feature.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by statistical analysis presented in the results.

claim: Mutations of genes predicted to have related functions led to similar behavioural differences in worms.
source: The observed phenotypes were diverse, but mutations of genes predicted to have related functions led to similar behavioural differences in worms.
evidence: This is supported by clustering analysis and specific examples like bbs-1, bbs-2, and tub-1 mutants.

claim: Two compounds (liranaftate and atorvastatin) rescued the behavioural phenotype of a model of UNC80 deficiency.
source: As a proof-of-concept, we performed a drug repurposing screen of an FDA-approved compound library, and identified two compounds that rescued the behavioural phenotype of a model of UNC80 deficiency.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the drug screen experiments.

claim: More than 300 million people worldwide are affected by rare genetic diseases.
source: However, because there are many kinds of rare diseases, they are collectively common and affect more than 300 million people worldwide (Nguengang Wakap et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Nguengang Wakap et al., 2020.

claim: Over 80% of rare genetic diseases affect children.
source: Over 80% of rare genetic diseases affect children and many have severe symptoms (Bavisetty et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Bavisetty et al., 2013.

claim: 95% of rare diseases have no approved treatment.
source: Furthermore, 95% of rare diseases have no approved treatment (Nguengang Wakap et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Nguengang Wakap et al., 2020.

claim: Genome and exome sequencing has become faster and cheaper, enabling its widespread use in the diagnosis of genetic diseases.
source: Genome and exome sequencing has become faster and cheaper, enabling its widespread use in the diagnosis of genetic diseases.
evidence: This is a statement about technological advances in genomics, drawing from established knowledge.

claim: Rapid identification of genetic lesions associated with rare genetic diseases has been enabled by genome and exome sequencing.
source: In turn, this has led to the rapid identification of genetic lesions associated with rare genetic diseases (Gonzaga-Jauregui et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Gonzaga-Jauregui et al., 2012.

claim: More than half of the human genes associated with rare genetic diseases in the OMIM database are conserved in C. elegans.
source: For the model nematode C. elegans, more than half of the human genes associated with rare genetic diseases in the OMIM database are conserved (Kropp et al., 2021)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kropp et al., 2021.

claim: CRISPR-based editing has made the generation of in vivo models containing disease-relevant mutations faster and easier.
source: and CRISPR-based editing has made the generation of in vivo models containing disease-relevant mutations faster and easier.
evidence: This is a statement about technological advances in genome editing, drawing from established knowledge.

claim: Pimozide improved clinical and physiological outcomes in ALS patients in early clinical trials.
source: Early clinical trials found pimozide improved clinical and physiological outcomes in ALS patients (Patten et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Patten et al., 2017.

claim: Epalrestat is currently being tested in clinical trials for PMM2-CDG patients.
source: One of the compounds, the aldose reductase inhibitor epalrestat, is currently being tested in clinical trials for PMM2-CDG patients (National Clinical Trial number: NCT04925960).
evidence: This is supported by a reference to a clinical trial number.

claim: Approximately 74% of rare genetic diseases affect nervous system function.
source: The majority (~74%) of rare genetic diseases affect nervous system function (Lee et al., 2020)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2020.

claim: 767 C. elegans genes with 2558 orthologous human protein-coding genes met the filtering criteria for disease model selection.
source: A total of 767 C. elegans genes with 2558 orthologous human protein-coding genes met these criteria (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a result from the gene filtering process, supported by data and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: 22 genes in the final panel have >60% sequence similarity to their human ortholog.
source: In the final panel of 25 worm genes selected, 22 genes have >60% sequence similarity to their human ortholog, and 11 of the genes share >90% sequence similarity to their human counterpart (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a result from sequence analysis, supported by data and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: 11 genes in the final panel share >90% sequence similarity to their human counterpart.
source: In the final panel of 25 worm genes selected, 22 genes have >60% sequence similarity to their human ortholog, and 11 of the genes share >90% sequence similarity to their human counterpart (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a result from sequence analysis, supported by data and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: 24/25 genes are predicted to be orthologous to human genes across >3 orthology prediction algorithms.
source: Furthermore, 24/25 genes are predicted to be orthologous to human genes across >3 orthology prediction algorithms (Figure 1C)
evidence: This is a result from orthology analysis, supported by data and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: All selected genes have a BLAST E-value smaller than 3×10–12.
source: and all selected genes have a BLAST E-value (McGinnis and Madden, 2004) smaller than 3×10–12 (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a result from sequence analysis, supported by data in Supplementary file 1.

claim: Large CRISPR-Cas9 deletions (mean 4.4 kb) were made in each of the target genes.
source: Large CRISPR-Cas9 deletions (mean 4.4 kb) were made in each of the target genes to generate 25 strains containing a >55% deletion (average 76%) of the chosen gene.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used to create the mutant strains.

claim: The 25 strains contain a >55% deletion (average 76%) of the chosen gene.
source: Large CRISPR-Cas9 deletions (mean 4.4 kb) were made in each of the target genes to generate 25 strains containing a >55% deletion (average 76%) of the chosen gene.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used to create the mutant strains.

claim: The mutated genes are associated with 31 rare genetic disorders in humans according to OMIM.
source: According to OMIM, the mutated genes are associated with 31 rare genetic disorders in humans including intellectual disability, developmental delay, and disorders affecting the muscular and/or nervous systems
evidence: This is based on information from the OMIM database.

claim: The mutated genes are associated with >70 clinical presentations of disease according to the Human Disease Ontology database.
source: and are associated with >70 clinical presentations of disease according to the Human Disease Ontology database (Schriml et al., 2022; Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is based on information from the Human Disease Ontology database, supported by citation.

claim: A single minutes-long recording can capture differences in morphology, posture, and behaviour that can classify the effect of mutations and drug treatments.
source: High-resolution worm tracking and behavioural fingerprinting is a promising candidate for a widely applicable assay because it is both fast and multidimensional: a single minutes-long recording can capture differences in morphology, posture, and behaviour that can classify the effect of mutations and drug treatments (Baek et al., 2002; Barlow et al., 2022; Geng et al., 2004; Javer et al., 2018b; McDermott-Rouse et al., 2021; Perni et al., 2018; Ramot et al., 2008; Restif et al., 2014; Swierczek et al., 2011; Tsibidis and Tavernarakis, 2007; Wang and Wang, 2013; Yemini et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: 2763 features covering morphology, posture, and motion are extracted for each recording.
source: For each recording, we extract 2763 features covering morphology, posture, and motion and concatenate the feature vectors together to represent the phenotype of each strain (8289 features in total).
evidence: This is a description of the data extraction methods used in the study.

claim: 8289 features in total are used to represent the phenotype of each strain.
source: For each recording, we extract 2763 features covering morphology, posture, and motion and concatenate the feature vectors together to represent the phenotype of each strain (8289 features in total).
evidence: This is a description of the data extraction methods used in the study.

claim: bbs-1, bbs-2, and tub-1 mutants affect cilia formation and result in similar phenotypes that cluster together.
source: For example, bbs-1, bbs-2, and tub-1 mutants affect cilia formation and result in similar phenotypes that cluster together.
evidence: This is a result from hierarchical clustering analysis, supported by data.

claim: kcc-2, snf-11 and unc-25 mutants all affect GABAergic function and result in similar phenotypes that cluster together.
source: The same is true for kcc-2, snf-11 and unc-25 mutants, which all affect GABAergic function.
evidence: This is a result from hierarchical clustering analysis, supported by data.

claim: 23 out of 25 disease model strains are significantly different from the wild-type in at least one feature.
source: From the panel of 25 disease model strains, 23 are significantly different from the wild-type in at least one feature (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by statistical analysis and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Some strains including bbs-1, bbs-2, glr-1, and unc-43 display a sustained photophobic response.
source: While most strains show a partial recovery in the post-stimulus recording, some strains including bbs-1, bbs-2, glr-1, and unc-43 display a sustained photophobic response (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a result from the behavioral analysis, supported by data and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Approximately 74% of rare genetic diseases affect nervous system function.
source: The majority (~74%) of rare genetic diseases affect nervous system function (Lee et al., 2020)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2020.

claim: 35 genes (6.4% of the total list) in the longlist of 543 disease genes were predicted to be involved in cilia function.
source: In the longlist of 543 disease genes, there were 35 genes (6.4% of the total list) predicted to be involved in cilia function.
evidence: This is a result from the gene filtering process.

claim: Mutations in BBS1 account for 23.4% of Bardet-Biedl syndrome cases.
source: The most prevalent BBS mutations are in BBS1, accounting for 23.4% of cases (Forsyth and Gunay-Aygun, 2023)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Forsyth and Gunay-Aygun, 2023.

claim: Mutations in BBS2 account for 8% of Bardet-Biedl syndrome cases.
source: Mutations in BBS2 account for 8% of BBS cases (Forsythe and Beales, 2013)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Forsythe and Beales, 2013.

claim: bbs-1(syb1588) and bbs-2(syb1547) mutants were shorter, wider, and had decreased curvature compared to wild-type worms.
source: bbs-1(syb1588) and bbs-2(syb1547) mutants were shorter, wider, and had decreased curvature compared to wild-type worms (Figure 3A, B and C).
evidence: This is a result from the phenotypic analysis, supported by data and shown in Figure 3.

claim: bbs-1(syb1588) and bbs-2(syb1547) mutants are hyperactive, with a greater fraction of worms moving during pre-stimulus recordings.
source: They are also hyperactive, with a greater fraction of worms moving during pre-stimulus (baseline) recordings (see individual gene cards)
evidence: This is a result from the phenotypic analysis, supported by data.

claim: bbs-1(syb1588) and bbs-2(syb1547) mutants had faster body bends compared to N2.
source: and had faster body bends (a derivative of curvature) compared to N2 (Figure 3D and F).
evidence: This is a result from the phenotypic analysis, supported by data and shown in Figure 3.

claim: BBS proteins regulate the C. elegans photoreceptor protein LITE1 in ASH sensory neurons through a DLK-MAPK signalling pathway independent of their function in cilia.
source: BBS proteins also regulate the C. elegans photoreceptor protein LITE1 in ASH sensory neurons through a DLK-MAPK signalling pathway independent of their function in cilia (Zhang et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2022.

claim: bbs-1(syb1588) and bbs-2(syb1547) mutants have attenuated blue light sensitivity.
source: Consistent with this, we find that bbs-1(syb1588) and bbs-2(syb1547) mutants have attenuated blue light sensitivity, with both strains exhibiting a delayed forward, but enhanced backward photophobic escape response upon 10 s stimulation with blue light (Figure 3F–H).
evidence: This is a result from the phenotypic analysis, supported by data and shown in Figure 3.

claim: tub-1(syb1562) mutants are shorter, wider, and hyperactive compared to wild-type worms.
source: tub-1(syb1562) mutants are shorter, wider, and hyperactive compared to wild-type worms, similar to bbs-1 and bbs-2 mutants (Figure 3A, B and E).
evidence: This is a result from the phenotypic analysis, supported by data and shown in Figure 3.

claim: tub-1(syb1562) mutants have a defect in their response to blue light.
source: They also have a defect in their response to blue light (Figure 3F–H).
evidence: This is a result from the phenotypic analysis, supported by data and shown in Figure 3.

claim: Cilia integrity is maintained in tub-1 loss-of-function mutants.
source: Unlike BBS mutants, cilia integrity is maintained in tub-1 loss-of-function mutants (Mak et al., 2006)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Mak et al., 2006.

claim: tmem-231 mutants do not have significant differences in body morphology or posture compared to N2.
source: However, unlike the other cilia-related mutants, tmem-231 mutants do not have significant differences in body morphology or posture compared to N2 (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a result from the phenotypic analysis, supported by data and shown in Figure 3.

claim: tmem-231(syb1575) is slightly more active during baseline tracking.
source: We do note that tmem-231(syb1575) is slightly more active during baseline tracking (see strain-specific gene card).
evidence: This is a result from the phenotypic analysis, supported by data.

claim: NALCN is expressed throughout the central nervous system, and in parts of the endocrine, respiratory and cardiac systems.
source: The Na + cation leak channel (NALCN) is expressed throughout the central nervous system, and in parts of the endocrine (pancreas, adrenal, thyroid gland), respiratory and cardiac systems (Cochet-Bissuel et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Cochet-Bissuel et al., 2014.

claim: NALCN is a voltage-independent, nonselective cation channel that regulates resting potential.
source: NALCN is a voltage-independent, nonselective cation channel that regulates resting potential (Senatore et al., 2013)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Senatore et al., 2013.

claim: NALCN plays a role in neuromodulation by neurotransmitters.
source: and plays a role in neuromodulation by neurotransmitters (Cochet-Bissuel et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Cochet-Bissuel et al., 2014.

claim: NALCN-knock-out mice die 12 hr after birth.
source: NALCN-knock-out mice die 12 hr after birth (Lu et al., 2007)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Lu et al., 2007.

claim: C. elegans encodes two functionally redundant, but differentially expressed, NALCN homologs, NCA-2 and UNC-77.
source: C. elegans encodes two functionally redundant, but differentially expressed, NALCN homologs, NCA-2 and UNC-77, whose proper expression and axonal localisation in cholinergic neurons are regulated by UNC-80 (Zhou et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Zhou et al., 2020.

claim: nca-2, unc-77, and unc-80 loss-of-function mutants are viable.
source: Unlike murine models, nca-2, unc-77, and unc-80 loss-of-function mutants are viable.
evidence: This is a result from the study, supported by the creation and analysis of these mutants.

claim: Loss-of-function mutations in nca-2 and unc-80 result in morphological changes in C. elegans: both mutants are significantly shorter than wild-type N2.
source: Similar to Drosophila melanogaster or mouse neonates lacking the cation leak channel (Cochet-Bissuel et al., 2014), loss-of-function mutations in nca-2 and unc-80 result in morphological changes in C. elegans: both mutants are significantly shorter than wild-type N2 (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a result from the phenotypic analysis, supported by data and shown in Figure 4.

claim: nca-2(syb1612) has no significant change in curvature, but is slower than the wild-type strain.
source: In contrast, nca-2(syb1612) has no significant change in curvature, but is slower than the wild-type strain (Figure 4B–C).
evidence: This is a result from the phenotypic analysis, supported by data and shown in Figure 4.

claim: unc-80(syb1531) mutants have the most severe phenotype exhibiting a decrease in both curvature and speed.
source: We find that unc-80(syb1531) mutants, which affect the localisation of NALCN channel subunits, have the most severe phenotype exhibiting a decrease in both curvature and speed (Figure 4B-C).
evidence: This is a result from the phenotypic analysis, supported by data and shown in Figure 4.

claim: Mutations in both NALCN channel subunits in C. elegans cause a 'fainter' phenotype when stimulated mechanically or immersed in liquid.
source: Mutations in both NALCN channel subunits in C. elegans cause a 'fainter' phenotype when stimulated mechanically or immersed in liquid (Pierce-Shimomura et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Pierce-Shimomura et al., 2008.

claim: A ten-second blue light pulse resulted in increased post-exposure pausing and a decreased forward escape response in nca-2(syb1612) and unc-80(syb1531) single mutants.
source: Similarly, we found that a ten-second blue light pulse resulted in increased post-exposure pausing and a decreased forward escape response in nca-2(syb1612) and unc-80(syb1531) single mutants (Figure 4E–H).
evidence: This is a result from the phenotypic analysis, supported by data and shown in Figure 4.

claim: unc-77(syb1688) mutants did not 'faint' after blue light exposure.
source: unc-77(syb1688) mutants did not 'faint' after blue light exposure
evidence: This is a result from the phenotypic analysis, supported by data.

claim: Both unc-77(syb1688) and unc-80(syb1531) fail to initiate a backward escape response.
source: but consistent with findings that the NALCN channel some regulates reversal behaviour (Zhou et al., 2020) both unc-77(syb1688) and unc-80(syb1531) fail to initiate a backward escape response.
evidence: This is a result from the phenotypic analysis, supported by data and citation.

claim: Pausing and 'fainting' after blue light exposure represent a novel screenable phenotype for NALCN-channelopathies.
source: Pausing and 'fainting' after blue light exposure represent a novel screenable phenotype for NALCN-channelopathies.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: A library of 743 FDA-approved drugs was used for the repurposing screen.
source: For the repurposing screen, we used a library of 743 FDA-approved drugs.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods.

claim: Drugs were tested at a final concentration of 100 μM with 1% DMSO.
source: We prepared tracking plates where each well contained a drug at a final concentration of 100 μM with 1% DMSO.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods.

claim: Testing larger feature sets reduced the power to detect differences in the drug screen.
source: To test the utility of reducing the feature set in a screen compared to testing a larger feature set, we repeated this with larger feature sets. Testing larger feature sets reduced our power to detect differences.
evidence: This is a result from the statistical analysis of the drug screen.

claim: No hits were detected using a predefined set of 256 features.
source: No hits were detected using a predefined set of 256 features (Javer et al., 2018b; Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a result from the statistical analysis of the drug screen, shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: 13 of the 30 hits were reproduced in the confirmation screen.
source: We then performed a confirmation screen on 30 of the hit compounds from the initial screen with a larger number of replicates (24 wells per day over three independent days). 13 of the 30 hits were reproduced in the sense of showing significant differences from unc-80 DMSO controls in the direction of wild-type
evidence: This is a result from the confirmation screen.

claim: About half of the confirmed hit compounds lead to more than 1000 side effects.
source: About half of the confirmed hit compounds lead to more than 1000 side effects (Figure 5C)
evidence: This is a result from the side effect analysis, shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Liranaftate and atorvastatin lead to good rescue of the core unc-80 behavioural phenotypes.
source: Of the confirmed hit compounds with fewer than 1000 side effects, liranaftate and atorvastatin (Lipitor) lead to good rescue of the core unc-80 behavioural phenotypes.
evidence: This is a result from the drug screen analysis.

claim: Both liranaftate and atorvastatin act upon the mevalonate biosynthesis pathway.
source: Interestingly, both compounds act upon the mevalonate biosynthesis pathway.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of the drug mechanisms of action.

claim: Atorvastatin is an inhibitor of HMG-CoA reductase that regulates lipid homeostasis.
source: Atorvastatin is an inhibitor of HMG-CoA reductase that regulates lipid homeostasis (Goldstein et al., 2006)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Goldstein et al., 2006.

claim: Liranaftate is an antifungal inhibitor of squalene epoxidase.
source: Liranaftate, an antifungal inhibitor of squalene epoxidase, shows the greatest behavioural improvement, with the fewest number of side effects.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of the drug mechanism of action and results from the drug screen.

claim: C. elegans lacks the branch of the mevalonate pathway responsible for converting squalene to cholesterol.
source: However, C. elegans lacks the branch of the mevalonate pathway responsible for converting squalene to cholesterol, instead relying on dietary cholesterol.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of C. elegans metabolism.

claim: Fenofibrate is a PPAR-alpha activator that increases lipolysis.
source: Fenofibrate, a PPAR-alpha activator that increases lipolysis, is also a hit but has a large number of side effects.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of the drug mechanism of action and results from the drug screen.

claim: Changes in membrane composition might be indirectly affecting the localisation or function of the NALCN channel complex.
source: Since UNC-80 is involved in localisation of the NACLN+ channel complex, we hypothesise that changes in membrane composition might be indirectly affecting the localisation or function of the channel complex.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the experimental results and knowledge of UNC-80 function.

claim: It is possible to systematically create and phenotype worm models of rare diseases using a uniform assay and protocol.
source: Using an initial set of genes that are diverse in function (but biased towards roles in neurons and muscles) and that lead to diverse symptoms when mutated in humans, we found that it is possible to systematically create and phenotype worm models of rare diseases using a uniform assay and protocol.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: 23 out of the 25 disease models had detectable differences compared to the wild-type.
source: Without adding additional perturbations or experimental conditions, we found that 23 out of the 25 disease models we made had detectable differences compared to the wild-type.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the study.

claim: Approximately half of the disease models with detectable phenotypes had strong phenotypes that would support high throughput phenotypic screens for candidate treatments.
source: Of the disease models with detectable phenotypes, approximately half had strong phenotypes that would support high throughput phenotypic screens for candidate treatments.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: The current discovery rate of new genetic diseases is >100 per year.
source: With a current discovery rate of >100 new genetic diseases each year, the number of diseases with little aetiological understanding is going to grow at a faster rate than biomedical and pharmaceutical research will find therapies (Boycott et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Boycott et al., 2017.

claim: CRISPR genome editing in model organisms including C. elegans allows the creation of new disease models at the required rate and cost.
source: CRISPR genome editing in model organisms including C. elegans allows the creation of new disease models at the required rate and cost.
evidence: This is a statement about the capabilities of CRISPR technology, drawing from established knowledge.

claim: High-throughput worm tracking can identify screenable phenotypes and be used for repurposing screens.
source: We have shown that high-throughput worm tracking can identify screenable phenotypes and be used for repurposing screens.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results of the study.
